feasibility_reasoning:
The mechanism is easy to build. scripts/check-bundle-size.ts:2472-2480 already computes bootRaw over bootClosure(files). Gating it means adding a FROZEN_BUDGET_KB key (:1752-2044), a budget('bootRaw','MAX_BOOT_RAW_KB') call (:2049-2073), an errors.push (:2571-2583), a headroom row (:2630-2637) and an optional BaselineFile.totals.bootRaw (:2117-2130, :2605-2613). The negative-control harness exists: src/lib/ci/__tests__/platformBuildGuards.test.ts:73-113 (a fixture plus MAX_BOOT_KB='1' plus entropy()), and existing tests stay green.

Five problems:
(1) :2476-2478 documents the choice not to gate raw ('Raportowane, NIE bramkowane - jedna metryka, jeden próg'), so the change needs a chronicle entry.
(2) The floor of 1568 KB + 0.5% was measured in the sandbox on build:smoke (vite.smoke.config.ts), but CI gates `bun run build` on the runner (.github/workflows/ci.yml:997,1052). The documented host-to-runner skew is +0.466% (:841, :1232), so a 0.5% margin is about 0.03% of real headroom, the same error the file admits at :2032-2041. The file's own formula gives 1568.6*1.00466 = 1575.9 -> 1577, re-floored from the first green runner log (wpis V).
(3) 'The real artifact passes' cannot be checked end to end, because check:bundle already exits 1 on main (overall 4806.8 > 4772).
(4) It duplicates the untracked scripts/performance/document-weight-budgets.json bootClosureRawBytes gate (max 1637758 B, measured 1605645 B = 1568.0 KB). That is two floors for one number.
(5) No SSR, hydration, i18n, SEO, CLS or chunk-graph risk, since this is a CI script only.
blocking_issues: The floor comes from sandbox build:smoke, but CI gates `bun run build` on the runner (ci.yml:997,1052). A 0.5% margin is below the file's own host-to-runner formula (+0.466% plus ceiling plus 1 KB, check-bundle-size.ts:1232), so it must be re-floored from a green runner log or the gate fires on noise.
It duplicates bootClosureRawBytes in the untracked scripts/performance/document-weight-budgets.json (max 1637758 B). Choose one gate, not two floors for the same quantity.
check-bundle-size.ts:2476-2478 documents the decision not to gate raw ('jedna metryka, jeden próg'). Overriding it needs a chronicle entry and a reason why a gzip ratchet is not enough.
check:bundle is already red on main (overall 4806.8 > 4772 KB), so 'the real artifact passes' can only be asserted as 'no boot-raw error line', not as exit 0.
effect_reasoning:
'No direct score change' is correct. The attribution 'raw bytes, so parse/compile on 4x CPU, so TBT/TTI' does not hold in Lighthouse's own data. bootup-time scriptParseCompile summed over .js URLs is about 8/3/2 ms in baseline2 mobile runs 1-3 (all scripts including the document: 91/40/39 ms), against 4064-5322 ms of scripting, of which vendor-react hydration is 4447 ms. prod-mobile.json shows 3 ms of JS parse/compile against 1533 ms of scripting, and desktop shows 0-3 ms. V8 streams and compiles module scripts off the main thread and compiles functions lazily. A +10% raw regression (+157 KB) therefore adds well under 1 ms of main-thread parse/compile, which is 0 TBT points.

The real risk from boot bytes is transfer at 1.6 Mb/s competing with the hero image for LCP (EVIDENCE §10). The existing gzip boot gate covers that but has 102 KB of slack (579 vs 477.1). Spending it costs 102*8/1600 ≈ 0.51 s of mobile bandwidth. A raw floor with 7.8 KB of slack (about 2.4 KB gzip at a raw/gzip ratio of 3.29) would bind before the gzip gate, so the binding gate would be the metric Lighthouse barely counts.

A cheaper and better change: ratchet FROZEN_BUDGET_KB.boot from 579 to 477.1*1.00466 = 479.3 -> 480 -> 481 KB gzip. It needs no new code, keeps one metric and one threshold, and guards transfer and, through the ratio, raw size.
corrected_estimate: 0 score points directly. As a guard, the raw gate is worth about 0 ms of TBT/TTI per realistic regression: Lighthouse attributes under 10 ms of parse/compile to all boot JS, and a +10% raw regression adds under 1 ms. Its only unique catches are highly compressible additions, and those also cost transfer. Ratcheting the gzip boot floor from 579 to 481 KB instead prevents up to about 0.5 s of silent mobile LCP or bandwidth drift (102 KB * 8 / 1.6 Mb/s) and makes the raw gate largely redundant. If the raw gate is added anyway, use a single gate with a runner-derived floor of about 1577 KB (1568.6*1.00466, ceiling, +1).
better_alternative: Ratchet the existing gzip boot budget from 579 to 481 KB, using the file's own +0.466% host-to-runner formula, then re-floor from the runner log. Keep bootRaw as a reported or headroom-warning line. If audit item 3.9 must be closed literally, keep only one raw gate: either check:bundle or the document-weight bootClosureRawBytes gate, not both.
